## August 24, 1931 — A Monday

On the exact day of your birth, the British government collapsed. Ramsay MacDonald's Labour Cabinet had been unable to agree on emergency budget cuts — the Depression had drained the Treasury, and the proposed solution was to cut unemployment benefits to people the Depression had already destroyed. MacDonald resigned on August 24th. King George V asked him to stay on and form a National Government, a coalition across party lines. MacDonald agreed, and his own Labour Party promptly expelled him for it. The British constitutional crisis of August 1931 resolved on the day you were born, in a way that satisfied almost nobody and held the country together anyway. A pattern recognizable across the entire century that followed.

---

**On August 24th, in the year 79, Vesuvius buried Pompeii.** The eruption began in the early afternoon and was finished by morning. A prosperous Roman city of perhaps eleven thousand people was sealed under meters of ash and pumice, preserved so completely that when excavators began uncovering it seventeen centuries later, they found bread still in the ovens. You share your birthday with the most famous catastrophe in classical history — a day that erased a world so thoroughly that the world had to be reinvented before anyone could find it again.

**The banking system of the Western world was coming apart around you.** The immediate trigger was not the 1929 crash but May 1931, when the Austrian bank Credit-Anstalt failed. The cascade that followed moved through Germany, then Britain, then the rest of Europe, each country's financial system pulling at the next. By August 1931, banks across the industrialized world were failing or teetering. Unemployment in the United States was climbing toward twenty percent. The monetary system that had organized global trade since the nineteenth century was dissolving. Three weeks after your birth, Britain abandoned the gold standard entirely — September 21, 1931. The economic world your parents had been born into no longer existed.

**Frankenstein was in production the year you were born.** Universal Pictures released Dracula in February 1931, six months before your birth, and Frankenstein in November 1931, three months after. Both were immediate cultural phenomena — horror as a genre, the monster as a figure for modern anxieties about science and death and the uncontrollable, crystallized in the year of your birth. The century's defining popular mythology was being assembled in Hollywood while the banks failed and the bread lines lengthened. People needed their monsters named and placed on a screen where they could be watched at a safe distance.

**You were born into the age of radio, not television.** In August 1931, television was a laboratory experiment. Radio was the nervous system of the modern world — Franklin Roosevelt's fireside chats, which would begin eighteen months after your birth, assumed a population gathered around radio receivers. The news of bank failures, dust storms, political crises, and the distant rumblings from Germany reached people through a box in the living room that produced only sound. You are among the last generation for whom radio was the primary mass medium of childhood — who heard the world before they saw it on a screen.

**The Dust Bowl was ten weeks from its first major storm.** The agricultural catastrophe that would displace hundreds of thousands of people from the Great Plains began, meteorologically, in November 1931 — its first great dust storm sweeping across the region. The conditions had been building for years: plowed-up grassland, drought, and the economic pressure of the Depression driving farmers to plant every acre they had. The Okies and Arkies who appeared in Steinbeck's *Grapes of Wrath* were not yet on the road when you were born, but they were months from starting.

**Al Capone was awaiting trial.** He had been indicted in June 1931 and would be convicted of tax evasion in October, sentenced to eleven years. The federal government had been unable to pin organized crime charges on him and had gone after his income taxes instead. The irony was not lost on anyone. In the year of your birth, the most famous criminal in America was brought down by accountants, which said something both about the Depression and about the nature of power.

---

**The arc of a lifetime.**

You are ninety-five years old in 2026.

Born before the New Deal, before Social Security, before the minimum wage. Born before penicillin was in clinical use, before the jet engine, before the atomic bomb. A child of the Depression who came of age precisely as the world went to war — Pearl Harbor happened when you were ten. You were fourteen at V-E Day, fourteen still at Hiroshima. The war that consumed your entire adolescence ended before you were old enough to fight in it.

From there: Korea, Sputnik, the Civil Rights movement, Kennedy's assassination at thirty-two, the moon at thirty-seven, Vietnam through your thirties and forties, Watergate at forty-one. The Berlin Wall fell when you were fifty-eight. The internet arrived in your sixties. September 11th when you were seventy. A smartphone when you were in your late seventies. A pandemic at eighty-eight.

The radio that was the medium of your childhood is now a nostalgia object. Frankenstein and Dracula have been remade so many times they have become parody. The gold standard MacDonald abandoned the month after your birth has been gone for ninety-four years and almost no one alive remembers its weight.

You have outlasted the entire twentieth century and most of its defining crises. The Monday in August when you arrived — the banks failing, the government collapsing in London, Vesuvius's anniversary passing as it always does — was the beginning of ninety-five years of a world that never stopped changing long enough to let anyone fully catch their breath.
